title: Angry customer
tagline: Learn to de-escalate furious callers, resolve their issue and keep the call professional.
you_are: a tier-one support agent handling inbound escalations
setting: Calls arrive in a busy contact centre; you wear a headset, read the account on screen and talk only by voice.

scenarios.label: Unexpected overage bill
scenarios.desc: A caller opens with rage over a surprise $300 charge they never authorised.
scenarios.setup: The caller is a freelance designer who just saw the charge on their banking app. They shout: You people stole three hundred dollars from me yesterday and I want it back right now.
scenarios.objective: Acknowledge the shock, verify the charge and secure agreement on the first corrective step.

scenarios.label: Third outage this month
scenarios.desc: A small-business owner faces the third internet outage in four weeks and threatens to cancel.
scenarios.setup: The caller runs a bakery with a broken POS system. They say: This is the third time in a month my card reader goes dark during rush hour. I am done. Cancel everything today.
scenarios.skills: Empathy under repeat-failure pressure and retention
scenarios.objective: Validate the business impact, present a credible recovery plan and keep the account active.

scenarios.label: Abusive caller demanding supervisor
scenarios.desc: A caller crosses into personal insults and refuses any troubleshooting unless a manager answers immediately.
scenarios.setup: The caller has been on hold twice. They snap: You are useless. Put a real human on the line or I sue. I know your name and where you sit.
scenarios.objective: Set a respectful boundary, warn once, then transfer to the supervisor queue with a concise hand-off note.

objections: I just want someone to fix this now
I’ve been on hold for half an hour
Your policy doesn’t help my problem
I’ve called before and nothing changes
You can’t do anything but read scripts
Your product broke and you won’t admit it
I need compensation now not excuses

rubric.label: Active listening
rubric.what: Paraphrase the caller’s core problem and emotion before offering any fix.

rubric.label: Empathetic acknowledgement
rubric.what: Use genuine phrases like I can hear how frustrating this is without adding but or policy language.

rubric.label: Ownership language
rubric.what: Say I am prioritising this right now or I will see this through instead of transferring blame.

rubric.label: Compliant apology
rubric.what: Apologise for the experience, not the policy, and never follow sorry with a limitation.

rubric.label: Boundary setting
rubric.what: Calmly state the behaviour you need to continue and the consequence if it persists.

rubric.label: Resolution clarity
rubric.what: Give one concrete next step, a time frame and a way to verify it happened.

pitfalls: Saying calm down or as per policy.
Threatening hang-up without a clear warning.
line: Calming down an angry customer as a support agent

research.text: To calm an angry customer, support agents should follow a clear de-escalation protocol: listen, acknowledge, apologize, confirm understanding, offer resolution, and follow through. Avoid phrases like “Calm down,” “As per our policy,” “There’s nothing I can do,” “That’s not our fault,” and any apology immediately followed by “but.” Instead, use phrases like “I’m prioritizing this right now” and “I can hear this has been a difficult experience.” If the customer’s behavior becomes abusive, agents should set firm but respectful boundaries and escalate to a supervisor. If harassment occurs, hanging up is appropriate. Use confident, empathetic tones and remain calm to de-escalate the situation.

personas.name: Vanessa Patel
personas.background: Vanessa joined the contact centre two years ago after moving to the city for a junior admin role. She handles billing complaints daily and tries to keep callers calm while learning the policies.
cares_about: getting the right information without jargon
not letting the call end with unresolved anger
pushbacks: I understand you’re frustrated, but I can only do what the system allows
I’m not ignoring you, I’m looking for the fastest solution
I will pass this on to someone who can adjust the charge if needed
wins_over: a clear next step that involves a real person
when they see I’m trying to find a fix rather than reciting policy
a genuine apology that isn’t scripted
